lens: DEFECTS & GATE HONESTY (phase-1 red team: H11 defects, adoption breakages, hardened gate, CI, coverage fuzz)

findings.title: A failing test that is skipped or deleted passes both record and compare: the 'every test passes except a dated allowlist' rule only looks at exit codes
findings.repro: Synthetic edits of a copy of gate/P1 (scratch p1_red_defects/gate_attacks.py, compare against an identical copy PREVX): S1 test_physics_forces.py rows skipped +2 with rc 0 (= @unittest.skip on the two LiftMonotonicityTests, the H11 defect-1 regression tests) -> compare PASS exit 0; S2 test_kernel_contracts.py rows removed in both modes (file deleted) -> PASS; S3 20 tests fewer in test_physics_settle.py -> PASS. Code: Gate.collect_tests sets G1/G1b/G8 from unexplained failures only; test_row records 'skipped' but nothing enforces it; compare_dirs prints 'ran X -> Y, skipped A -> B' and 'test file ... is gone' as information. A module-level unittest.SkipTest behaves the same (rc 0, ran 0).
findings.fix: Record per-test outcomes (unittest result ids, incl. skips and expected failures) in tests.json; in record and compare fail on any test id that disappears, becomes skipped / expectedFailure, or a test file that is gone or ran fewer tests, unless the committed allowlist has a dated 'skip' entry or the main session signs a 'test-removal' row (same second-signature scheme as spec edits).

findings.title: A partial re-run ('record --only X') merges with the earlier run's results and becomes a complete hand-over: checks run on different trees combine into PASS, and nothing ties a record to the tree
findings.repro: cp gate copy BASE -> gates/STALE (all checks PASS, stands for an earlier run); then python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py --gates-root <scratch>/gates record --id STALE --package P1 --prev PREVX --only G10 --work <scratch>/work_stale -> 'TIER1-GATE STALE [P1-ALL] vs PREVX: PASS'; meta.json: recorded = all 13 checks, partial None, last_run ['G10'], started kept from the old run, verdict PASS, handover true, G2 rows byte-identical to the old run. Gate.write: recorded = union(before, selected); checks = old checks updated with this run's. compare never checks that the record's fingerprints / git state match the working tree, so a record made before a regressing edit also still compares PASS. The pattern is used in practice: gate/ADOPT's meta has last_run ['G10'] (2.1 s) on top of earlier runs.
findings.fix: Store a tree fingerprint with every check result (audit code fingerprint + sha256 of tasks/authored, tests/ and house_sim/, or the git diff hash) and let a record be a hand-over only when every check carries the current tree's fingerprint; compare recomputes the fingerprint and reports STALE (FAIL) for a record that does not match the tree it is run on.

findings.title: The standalone compare (the final step tier1_adopt.js prescribes; exit 0 = PASS) passes records whose own verdict is FAIL: missing G0/G5/G7/G8 data and the record's own G0/G1b/G7/G8 statuses are ignored, and a narrowed PREV silently narrows G2-ABS
findings.repro: Copies of gate/P1 vs identical PREVX (gate_attacks.py): S5 meta G1b SKIP + G8 FAIL, rows absent -> compare PASS; S6 bench.json without G7, meta G7 SKIP -> PASS; S7 fingerprints {} and meta G0 SKIP -> PASS; S8 55 of 60 generation-1 digests and the layout counts absent -> PASS. Narrowed previous record: PREVN = PREVX with meta spec_files 'cleaning__*': python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py --gates-root <scratch>/gates compare PREVN E1_new_failing_spec -> 'G2 PASS 80 trials vs 80 ... compare result: PASS' (not INCOMPLETE) for a new spec failing every seed; compare ADOPTN P1 (ADOPT narrowed the same way) no longer reports G2-ABS for T-7d4006bda247ba-01. (record itself computes G2-ABS over all rows and keeps the failing statuses, so the record's meta verdict is FAIL; only compare disagrees.) RECORD_ONLY = (G1c, G9, G10); spec_scope() takes the previous meta's spec_files; record --prev accepts a narrowed record (default_prev_dir excludes them, an explicit --prev does not).
findings.fix: compare: every check the record lists in 'recorded' whose data compare cannot recompute counts with its own status (FAIL/SKIP fail), missing G0/G5/G7/G8 data for a recorded check is SKIP; G2-ABS always over the current record's full own-mode rows; a narrowed PREV (or CUR) makes the result INCOMPLETE; record --prev refuses a narrowed or partial record.

findings.title: Policy files can be forged in an isolated copy: the gate trusts the copy's own manifest, which is writable and excluded from the copy's change list (also hides any edited file from G10)
findings.repro: python <scratch>/policy_forge.py: a folder with .tier1_isolate.json whose base_files list the sha256 of a forged gate_policy/known_failing.json, a forged signoffs file and an edited house_sim/kernel/evaluation.py. python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py --root <fake> policy -> 'isolated copy, unchanged since its base commit' with the forged entries; python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py --root <fake> scope --package ADOPT:cleaning -> 'G10 PASS 0 changed file(s)'; python tools/orchestration/tier1_gate.py --root <fake> --gates-root <scratch>/gates compare PREVX E1_new_failing_spec -> PASS (exit 1 with the real repository's policy). No git commit is needed; --root also lets whoever runs compare choose the policy source.
findings.fix: Keep the isolate manifest outside the copy (in the project's gate folder, written by the main session) or seal it with a key the copy does not hold; read policy files from the project's git object store at the copy's base commit (git show <base>:path in the project repo), never from the copy; print and record the policy root, and have compare refuse a --root other than the project unless the main session passes an explicit flag.

findings.owner: house_sim/tasks/verify.py (wrong-plan evidence; VERIFY_HARDENING 14.3 rule 1 is the planned fix)
findings.title: Wrong plans that never act still count as evidence: unknown action names and fully refused steps pass; the phase-1 crash rule only covers exceptions that escape the lenient runner
findings.repro: Scratch copies of A-04b40946bea880-01 with one wrong plan each (make_wrong_specs.py + inline): python -m house_sim --check <scratch>/wrong_W9_do_unknown_action.json --seeds 0 1 2 41 97 (plan [{'do': 'frobnicate', 'target': '{clutter_1}'}]) -> PASS; wrong_W8_do_refused.json (two pick_up steps out of reach, both refused) -> PASS. Crashes are correctly not evidence: W1/W2/W5 (unknown step kind), W3 (TypeError in a skill), W4 (unbound template), W6 (crash after the mistake), W7 (KeyError) -> FAIL. Cause: verify.run_wrong_plan runs Runner(strict=False), which turns refusals and skill PlanErrors into runner.failures, so ran=True. Scale today: the P1 record has 443 of 3,190 own-mode wrong-plan trials with refused steps (121 plans), 123 trials with refusals >= their top-level steps (some refusals are the intended mistake). No authored plan names an unknown action today (static scan), so this is a hole for new specs.
findings.fix: Interim (does not contradict VERIFY_HARDENING): a wrong plan with an 'Unknown action' refusal or an argument-category refusal is not evidence; validate 'do' action names against the registry when a spec loads. Then VERIFY_HARDENING 14.3 rule 1 (a refused step allowed only inside 'mistake' or with an expect 'strict:' pattern).

findings.owner: safety (systems/safety/glass.py glass_system) + manipulation (common.reveal_breaks); kernel phys/impact.py floor_hazard
findings.title: Wrap containment, hand-back path: when a contained broken glass is unwrapped on the floor no domain scatters the pieces and no floor hazard appears
findings.repro: python <scratch>/probe_glass2.py, case 'wrapped: throw, then unwrap on the floor': a newspaper-wrapped glass thrown hard (contained: 0 shards, correct), then approach, crouch, unwrap -> jar broken, shattered True, contained False, floor_hazard None, 0 shard entities, 0 sharp floor hazards; the unwrapped control leaves floor_hazard 'sharp' on the jar and 15 shards (8 sharp floor hazards). Same with a scripted drop (probe_glass.py 'contained break then unwrap'). PHYSICS.md section 4: 'once the wrap or the packaging comes off they are the domain's to scatter'; manipulation.reveal_breaks sets shattered first, safety.glass_system only shatters broken items that are not yet shattered, and impact.break_entity sets floor_hazard only at break time.
findings.fix: A kernel 'containment ended' step (impact.uncontained(w, eid)) that gives the item its floor hazard and fires a phys hook the safety domain answers with its shard field; reveal_breaks calls it instead of only setting shattered; extend CrossLayerContractTests with the unwrap case.

findings.title: CI will be red on its first runs for reasons unrelated to regressions: wall-clock test bounds flake under the workflow's parallel load, and the spec sample's seed hits the known failing spec
findings.repro: CI emulation (HOME/USERPROFILE in scratch, HOUSE_AI_FORBID_NETWORK=1, PYTHONUTF8=1): python tools/orchestration/green_tests.py 3 --json <scratch>/green_tests_ci.json -> 4,643 tests, 127 of 128 runs ok, exit 1: test_camera_realism DeterminismTests.test_geometric_realistic_observe_overhead_is_small (strict) 'AssertionError: 0.01076 not less than 0.01' (passes 2/2 alone). The workflow runs 4 test processes on 4-vCPU runners; test_perception's overhead test and test_mind's 3 ms bound are the same kind (K-GATE saw them fail under load). The spec-sample step runs seed 41, on which T-7d4006bda247ba-01 fails (re-checked: seeds 0 and 41 'damage'), so run_check exits 1; CI reads no allowlist.
findings.fix: Move wall-clock bounds behind an opt-in flag (or a separate non-blocking perf job) and run them in the gate's quiet G7 bench instead; let the CI spec step honour the committed known_failing.json (or mark the step continue-on-error until T-7d4006 is fixed) so a red CI means a new regression.

findings.title: Lift monotonicity still breaks for damp or wet surfaces: a damp item slips one-handed from 4.8 kg while the same item at 8.01 kg is held with two hands
findings.repro: python <scratch>/probe_lift_damp.py (the K-FIX test scene): wetness 0.1 or 0.15 (damp) -> one-hand drop from 4.800 kg; wetness 0.3 -> from 3.200 kg; 8.01 kg -> held with both hands. grip_outcome at 6 kg damp: applied 52.3 N, required 65.4 N, slip, although the hand's hardware limit is 150 N (the adaptive cap is the rated DRY squeeze). probe_lift.py: 'damp surface' non-monotone masses 6.0-8.0 for humanoid_v1 and mobile_manipulator. Outside the documented contract (PHYSICS.md 8: 'clean, dry'), but the same planner-picks-a-lift-its-physics-fails class as H11 defect 1.
findings.fix: Let the adaptive one-hand grip rise to the hardware limit (body.grip_limit_n) for the surface it actually grips, or have lift_plan consult grip_outcome / the surface state and choose two hands; add a damp case to LiftMonotonicityTests.

findings.title: A second, undocumented camera-dependent privacy count: looking into a bathroom through an open doorway counts 1 with the geometric camera and 0 in room mode
findings.repro: python <scratch>/probe_privacy.py, case 'showering in bath, robot waits in the hall facing the doorway' (move hall, look, wait 300 s; scene from tests/test_kernel_contracts.py config): room 0, geometric 1, in oracle and realistic perception. Walk-in, walk out/in, two people, privacy mode and a 30-min stay agree between modes. KNOWN_LIMITS section 6 and K-FIX claim one remaining case only (a robot already in the room when the moment begins).
findings.fix: Either count a doorway view of a private moment in room mode too (people: the robot in a room connected by an open doorway, facing it) or document it in KNOWN_LIMITS and add it to CameraModeHarmTests as an expected difference before D3 makes geometric the default.

findings.owner: people / manipulation (hot hand-over harm owner); catalog/analysis/phase1/breakages.json
findings.title: Adoption breakage 9 residual not carried forward: one hot hand-over raises two global harm flags (injury from people, burns from manipulation)
findings.repro: tests.test_manipulation Mini scene: a 70 C mug handed to an adult (hand_over mug ana) -> stats {'burns': 1, 'injury': 1}, failure labels ['injury', 'burns']; other burn paths (coffee, kettle, oil scalds) count burns only. Filed only as an 'optional' request in manipulation.json (requests[4]); not in breakages.json or STATUS.md open items. HandOverTests pins the double count.
findings.fix: One owner per harm: manipulation steps aside when people's _hot_handover hook is loaded (or people counts burns only); list the item in breakages.json until done.

findings.title: The coverage fuzz counts no-op successes as 'driven to success': at least 4 of the 286 actions never changed anything when they 'succeeded'
findings.repro: python <scratch>/coverage_messages.py (the two coverage passes with success messages kept; same 286/427): open_valve 28 successes, all 'It is already fully open' / 'already at least that far open'; scrape and treat_upholstery only '(main: no change)' on cloths and tools; degrease one '(main: no change)'. Coverage numbers themselves reproduce exactly (see notes).
findings.fix: Count a success only when the step changed the world digest (or report no-op successes separately) and add the no-op-only actions to the never-succeeded list the domains are asked to cover.

findings.title: room_golden pins a known failing reference: T-7d4006bda247ba-01 seed 0 is recorded with passes false
findings.repro: tests/data/room_golden.json specs['T-7d4006bda247ba-01'] = {'passes': false, ...}; its history entry says so. G8 therefore treats the scorch as the expected outcome, and manipulation's fix will fail G8 until another re-record. (The three H11 defects are not pinned: see closed.)
findings.fix: golden.py refuses to record a failing reference unless the spec is on the committed allowlist, and stores it as 'known failing' so the fix shows as an expected golden change.

closed: H11 defect 1 (one-hand drop near the limit): fixed. probe_lift.py: humanoid_v1, mobile_manipulator and humanoid_compact x default, film, glass, steel, plastic, aluminium, handle, empty liquid jug, 17 masses 0.5-20 kg, each picked up then held 120 s and walked to another room and back: no dry case non-monotone, no accepted lift dropped. Regression tests (LiftMonotonicityTests, LiftPlanMatchesCorePickUpTests tightened, not loosened) pass normal and HOUSE_SIM_STRICT=1.

H11 defect 2 (wrapped-glass shards): fixed for the break itself. Scripted 1 m and 2.5 m drops wrapped in newspaper 1.0 / 0.95, clear plastic, a plain wrapped flag and intact packaging, and a robot hard throw (wrapped, clear plastic, packaged): 0 shard entities, 0 sharp floor hazards; coverage 0.949 and unwrapped controls shatter (15 shards) as the contract says. Residual on the unwrap path: see the wrap-containment finding.

H11 defect 3 (privacy double count): fixed for walking in. Walk in, walk out and back in, two people dressing, walking through the hall into a showering bathroom, privacy mode on, a 30-min stay: identical privacy and global-flag counts in room and geometric mode, oracle and realistic perception. Residual doorway case: see the camera-dependent privacy finding.

Not baked into goldens / tests: the H11 tests were tightened (test_physics_forces diff), test_camera.py (the both-camera-modes capture test) is unchanged since HEAD and passes; tests/data/room_golden.json pins none of the three paths (no privacy/shard/drop fields; T-7d4006 aside, see the golden finding) and test_room_golden passes on the fixed tree (normal and strict, CI emulation), so the goldens hold post-fix behaviour. Regression tests ran green: LiftMonotonicity, LiftPlanMatchesCorePickUp, CrossLayerContractTests, FallAndBreakTests, CameraModeHarmTests, CaptureTests (27 tests normal + strict).

Adoption breakages (adopt_status.json, 24): closed with regression tests by the owning domain or INT: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22 (cleaning + mechanisms aligned trigger_bottle; cleaning's not_fixed note about it is stale), 23; I re-ran 51 of their tests (safety Phase1Stabilise, people strike, mechanisms Phase1Stabilise, navigation sleeping dog, electrical router): OK. Closed for their domain with the spec failure carried forward: 0 and 1 (admin_inventory, appliances_cooking; T-7d4006 still fails seeds 0 and 41 via manipulation, breakages.json row 0, re-checked). 12 closed with the new two-draw residual listed (breakages.json row 6). 21 listed (INT not_fixed camera item, textiles_laundry not_fixed). 9 closed, residual not listed (see the hot hand-over finding).

Gate rules that hold (synthetic edits of P1 copies, real compare): E0 carried failure, E1 new spec failing every seed, E2 PASS->FAIL with the package's own reviewed.json (also blocked by G2-ABS even when signed), E4 edited spec with unchanged verdicts, spec trials removed, realistic trials removed, record's own G10 SKIP, 3 fuzz defects, coverage variant missing: all FAIL. Working-tree edits of gate_policy are ignored in the git work tree ('policy' reads HEAD; nothing committed yet). compare --spec-files narrowing ends INCOMPLETE as documented.
Crashing wrong plans are not evidence: TypeError in a skill, an unbound template, an unknown plan step kind, a KeyError and a crash after the mistake all fail the spec with the not_evidence message.

Compiled tasks/specs.jsonl matches tasks/authored (243/243 specs identical); the 9 edited specs are all visible to the gate (spec_hash changed) and in P1_signoff_draft; 196 of the 199 own-mode verdict rows vs ADOPT are variant swaps, 2 FAIL->PASS, 1 re-authored wrong plan (T-ce25a2474ffb3d-01).

Coverage fuzz numbers reproduce exactly: tools/fuzz.py --coverage --workers 4 -> 243 houses, 44,316 commands, 31,036 succeeded, 286 of 427 actions, 1 distinct defect (inspect closely heft grant, T-ab9a26cd6a795e-01 seed 97, admin_inventory, already in breakages.json row 1), 0 nondeterministic; equal to gate/P1 audits G6 'coverage'.

CI workflow: LF, no tabs, balanced expressions, valid structure by inspection; green_tests.py and run_check.py accept every argument used; the git-committing test sets a local identity; no Python 3.10+ runtime API found outside the AST guard's list.
notes: Lens: defects and gate honesty. Everything ran on the integrated tree of 2026-10-22 on a quiet machine; probes, gate copies and logs are in <home>\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-USER-OneDrive-Desktop-house-ai\e86e18f6-923d-4bcc-93e1-ba70c8993bc5\scratchpad\p1_red_defects (gate_attacks.py, policy_forge.py, probe_*.py, coverage_messages.py, make_wrong_specs.py, breakage_map.py, edited_specs.py). No project file was edited, nothing committed, nothing under %USERPROFILE%\.house_ai (the CI emulation ran with HOME/USERPROFILE in scratch), no network. Not run: the random-mode fuzz (it writes transient files under tools/), a real Linux / Python 3.9 run (no 3.9 interpreter here; no PyYAML, so the YAML check is structural). CI emulation (green_tests.py 3 with the workflow's env, Windows / Python 3.14): 4,643 tests, 127 of 128 runs ok, 1 wall-clock failure under load (see the CI finding); test_room_golden and every H11 regression test file green in both modes. Expected first CI result: the spec-sample step fails on T-7d4006bda247ba-01 (fails on seed 41, the CI seed; CI does not read known_failing.json). The four tier1_gate.py findings are about who can make the gate say PASS; the strongest fix for the stale-merge, compare and policy findings is that the main session itself runs 'record' for every hand-over on a clean tree and compares that record, with per-check tree fingerprints.
